text:
Sara: Quick update - ran a focused microbatch sweep on A6000 comparing streaming-chat (partial flush) vs sync completions. Found a nasty p99 knee when streaming microbatch > 4; want a triage meeting.

Michael: Cool, can you paste the headline p95/p99 and tokens/sec?

Sara: TL;DR (median of 10 runs, 2k tokens each):
- Streaming chat (partial flush): mb=1 => p95=85ms p99=210ms throughput=420k tok/s
- Streaming chat: mb=4 => p95=95ms p99=320ms throughput=540k tok/s
- Streaming chat: mb=8 => p95=130ms p99=680ms throughput=660k tok/s

- Sync completions (no streaming): mb=1 => p95=70ms p99=150ms throughput=380k tok/s
- Sync completions: mb=8 => p95=110ms p99=220ms throughput=780k tok/s

Observation: sync path scales smoothly as mb increases; streaming path shows superlinear tail degradation past ~4.

Anya: Do you have kernel-selection traces? Could be the runtime flipping kernels when the aggregate active tokens cross heuristics.

Sara: Pasted a short perf trace snippet where we saw a kernel flip: 
```
[trace] steps 0..3: GEMM-kernel-v2 (fast)
[trace] step 4: switch -> fused-attention-kernel
[trace] steps 5..n: GEMM-kernel-v2
[metric] kernel_switch_cost_ms=18.7
[metric] kv_cache_evictions=0
```

Michael: ~19ms switching cost fits the p99 bump. Is the trigger seq-length crossing or aggregate batch active tokens?

Sara: It looks like aggregate active tokens in the microbatch cause the fused kernel selection. With streaming + partial flush, per-request seq lengths vary, so at mb=8 brief sub-batches exceed threshold and flip kernels.

Devon: KV cache behavior? Streaming should reuse prefixes but partial flush can cause lock contention.

Sara: KV hit-rate remained ~96% but mutex wait increased noticeably: 
```
mutex_wait_kv_ms = 4.1 (mb=1)
mutex_wait_kv_ms = 16.8 (mb=8, streaming)
```
So more KV lookup stalls line up with the tail.

Anya: So two factors: kernel-switch tax + KV lookup contention. Together they cause superlinear p99.

Michael: Can you reproduce with synthetic uniform seq lengths to separate variance vs threshold?

Sara: Did that. With uniform seq=512 and streaming enabled, microbatch up to 16 scaled well and p99 stayed ~250ms. So variance in request lengths is the trigger, not just batch size.

Devon: Good repro. Possible mitigations?

Sara: Proposed mitigations: tighten kernel-selection hysteresis (avoid flip-flop), cap streaming microbatch default to 4, and add KV lock sharding or more lock-free lookups.

Michael: Also a soft-routing fallback: if kernel_switch_cost > 10ms and p99 creeping up, route streaming to lower-batch lane.

Sara: Mock config for experiment:
```
runtime:
  microbatch_max: 8
  per_route_overrides:
    streaming_chat:
      microbatch_max: 4
      kernel_hysteresis_ms: 30
      kv_lock_shards: 8
```

perf-bot: Deploy queued: canary runtime/patch/batch-hysteresis -> eng-runtime-canary (id: cb-2026-03-17-001)

Anya: If we set streaming default to mb=4, what's the throughput hit? Product will ask.

Sara: From the sweep: streaming mb=4 => 540k tok/s vs mb=8 => 660k tok/s => ~18% throughput drop. But p99 improves 680ms -> 320ms.

Michael: 18% fewer tokens/s but avoids p99 SLO violations/retries; probably worth it for latency-sensitive endpoints. Need cost calc though.

Devon: Recommend adaptive policy: start at mb=4 and only expand to 8 after sliding-window variance of seq lengths is low for N seconds (e.g., 30s). That keeps throughput when variance is low.

Sara: Proposed adaptive algo: track per-worker variance of seq lengths; bump cap only if var < threshold for 30s. Emit metrics: seq_var, mb_cap.

Michael: Any linkage to recent fused-attention heuristic change? I noticed a commit earlier this week around kernel selection thresholds.

Sara: We bisected. A tweak to fused-attention heuristics lowered the threshold so fused kernel was selected more often in mixed-length workloads. Reverting that change locally restored previous p99 behavior.

Anya: Action items:
- Sara: PR for per-route streaming default mb cap + kernel hysteresis (ETA EOD)
- Devon: prototype KV lock sharding (simple mod by shard id) and bench (ETA 2d)
- Michael: add adaptive variance-driven batch policy to roadmap + perf harness (ETA next week)
- Infra: watch canary and add kernel_switch events + kv_lock_wait per route

Sara: I'll add a synthetic high-variance streaming test to nightly perf and drop raw traces in perf-bucket.

perf-bot: canary deployed to eng-runtime-canary at 1773005700

Michael: Good thread. If canary looks stable, cut a hotfix for streaming defaults. Thanks all :raised_hands:

Sara: Ping me for traces or scripts, will upload to perf-bucket.
